stem: Which paediatric airway feature means an infant epiglottis should not be assumed to be adult-like?

options.text: It is longer, floppier, and narrower
It is the narrowest fixed point of the airway
It explains the winter peak of infections
It improves oxygen offload to tissues

explanation: The correct answer is that the infant epiglottis is longer, floppier, and narrower than in adults. This paediatric difference is the key reason adult upper-airway assumptions do not apply.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Respiratory 3.1 Acute Respiratory Problems

optionExplanations.A: Correct because the infant epiglottis is described as longer, floppier, and narrower than the adult epiglottis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the paediatric epiglottis is not shorter and wider.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the cricoid cartilage, not the epiglottis, is the narrowest fixed point of the paediatric airway.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because winter infection patterns relate to respiratory infections, not epiglottic anatomy.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because improved oxygen offload is related to fetal haemoglobin, not epiglottic shape.
